blocks.heading: A peel is not a stronger skincare step — it is a different kind of thing
quotes: “I saw how bright people looked afterwards, so I bought a kit to do it myself.”

explainer.heading: It has a start and a stop — which is what separates it from every other step
body: Everything else on this site is care: cleansing, hydrating, shielding, delivering actives gradually over weeks. A peel deliberately sheds the surface layer over a short window, which makes it a course with an end, not a habit.
The manufacturer designed this kit for three days, and three days means three days. Extending it because the peeling looks incomplete is the fastest route from a controlled course to an injury.

And because it removes part of the protective surface, the period straight afterwards is when skin is most vulnerable. Sun protection during that window is not advice but a precondition — if you cannot avoid sun over the next two weeks, postpone the peel.

blocks.heading: Five cases where this kit is not for you
blocks.intro: This is the strongest product on the site, so this section sits right below the first screen rather than hidden at the bottom.

items.heading: Pregnant or breastfeeding
items.body: This product contains retinol. That is an important difference from everything else here — the pigmentation combo uses bakuchiol precisely to avoid retinoids.

items.heading: Damaged skin, or skin affected by corticosteroid creams
items.body: Thin skin, visible vessels, active irritation or a recent procedure all need recovery first. Peeling over a weakened barrier makes it worse.

items.heading: Unable to use sunscreen daily
items.body: After peeling, skin is markedly more sensitive to sunlight. Without daily protection this course does more harm than good.

items.heading: Already using prescription retinoids or strong acids
items.body: Stacking several agents at once is the fastest way to break the skin barrier. Ask a doctor first.

items.heading: An important event within two weeks
items.body: Skin will be dry, tight and may darken temporarily before it flakes. Do not start a course right before an occasion where you want your skin at its best.

blocks.heading: Three days of peeling: what is normal, and when to stop
blocks.intro: This kit only works over three days. Knowing how your skin will react means you will not panic at what is normal — or brush off what is not.

items.label: Before day 1
items.body: Re-read the list of who should not use it. Have sunscreen ready, make sure you can arrange two low-sun weeks, and have no important occasion in the next two weeks.

items.label: Days 1–3: once a day
items.body: Cleanse, apply the peel and massage for 3–5 minutes, leave it on for up to 45 minutes (shorter the first time), rinse, then use the recovery ampoule and moisturiser. Three days means three days.

items.label: Normal during the course
items.body: Mild stinging on application. Dryness and tightness afterwards. Skin may darken temporarily before it flakes.

items.label: Stop immediately
items.body: Persistent stinging, swelling, blistering or pain. If redness deepens or the skin weeps, stop and see a doctor. None of these are in the normal group.

items.label: Days 3–10: shedding and recovery
items.body: Gentle cleansing, moisturiser and sunscreen only. No strong actives, no exfoliation, and do not pick at the flaking.

items.label: Up to day 21: strict sun avoidance
items.body: New skin darkens very readily. From day 14, once sensitivity and flaking have ended, you can return to your usual actives.

blocks.footnote: The days come from the manufacturer’s instructions for the three-day course and from the post-peel care in the schedule below. Skin differs from person to person.

blocks.heading: Three days of treatment, and the two weeks after that decide the outcome
blocks.intro: Most people plan the three days and forget what follows. What follows is longer, and getting it wrong wastes the three days entirely.

items.label: The peel course
items.note: Three days exactly as the enclosed instructions state. Do not extend it.

items.label: Shedding and recovery
items.note: Skin peels and is sensitive. Gentle cleansing, moisturiser and sunscreen only. No strong actives, no exfoliation, and do not pick at the flaking.

items.label: Strict sun avoidance
items.note: New skin darkens very readily. This is where a course goes from an improvement to worse pigmentation than before.

items.label: Return to your usual actives
items.note: Once sensitivity and flaking have ended. Going back sooner puts actives into a barrier that has not finished rebuilding.

blocks.footnote: These markers come from the manufacturer's instructions for the three-day course and from standard post-peel care. Skin differs from person to person, and if stinging persists, redness deepens, or the skin weeps, stop and see a doctor — that is no longer a normal response.
blocks.transition: The schedule only holds if the technique is right. Below is the three-day course, step by step.

blocks.heading: A three-day course, once a day
blocks.intro: The timings and the number of days are taken verbatim from the manufacturer. This is not a long-term daily product.

items.heading: Cleanse
items.body: Wash with the cleanser in the kit and dry.

items.heading: Apply the peel, massage 3–5 minutes
items.body: Spread evenly and massage gently for three to five minutes.

items.heading: Leave on for up to 45 minutes
items.body: The time depends on your skin. On a first session, stay well under the maximum.

items.heading: Rinse, then recover and protect
items.body: Rinse with clean water, use the recovery ampoule and the moisturiser. Sunscreen the next day is mandatory.

blocks.footnote: The manufacturer describes what is normal during the course: mild stinging on application, dryness and tightness afterwards, and skin possibly darkening temporarily before it flakes. But persistent stinging, swelling, blistering or pain means stop immediately — none of those are in the normal group.

items.q: Why does the pigmentation combo avoid retinoids while this contains retinol?
items.a: Because they do different jobs. The combo is a multi-week daily routine, so it uses bakuchiol to limit cumulative irritation. The peel is a three-day course with a defined end, accepting stronger action over a short period. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, this kit is not for you. The combo contains no retinoid, but in that period you should still ask your doctor before using anything.

items.q: How often can I repeat it?
items.a: We do not quote a figure, because the manufacturer does not publish an interval between courses. Ask an adviser or a dermatologist before repeating — peeling too frequently is a common cause of thinned skin.

items.q: Is it normal for skin to darken after peeling?
items.a: The manufacturer describes this as normal, with tone evening out as the skin flakes. But if it comes with persistent stinging, swelling or pain, that is something else and you should stop.

items.q: Can I use it alongside the pigmentation combo?
items.a: Not at the same time. Stacking a peel course on top of a pigment routine is the fastest way to break the skin barrier. Pick one, finish it, then consider the other.
